# 70-467 - Machine Learning for Business Analytics

::: {.hero-instructor}
**Instructor:** Andrés Castaño Zuluaga
:::

::: {.hero-lead}
Welcome to 70-467 Machine Learning for Business Analytics!
:::

::: {.hero-sub}
In an era when AI can write code faster than most people, writing code is not the scarce skill. The bottleneck in productive analytics is **understanding**, **verification**, and **judgment**: knowing what to ask the tools to do, checking whether the answer is good enough to act on, and explaining both the recommendation and its limits. AI will not replace your job. Someone who can use it and is prepared to work those bottlenecks will.

This course prepares you for that. You cannot evaluate the tools, or incorporate them into how you work, until you understand the methods. That is what sharpens judgment and makes the communication defensible. We incentivize responsible use of AI: tools that augment you, not substitutes that replace the thinking. You will learn to turn data into decisions you can stand behind. Choose the method, check it carefully, and explain the recommendation and its limits. The emphasis is business judgment under real problems, not model fitting as an end in itself. We work in R, with real datasets.
:::

## Methods you will see and use

We move from simple, interpretable models to richer tools, always starting from a **business problem** and emphasizing business **understanding**, method feasibility and limitations, and **judgement** in decision-making.

## How we work

A simple weekly rhythm so you always know how to prepare.

```{=html}
<div class="path-grid-proto path-grid-2x2 path-with-icons">
  <div class="path-card-proto">
    <span class="path-icon" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" width="28" height="28" fill="none"><rect x="6" y="4" width="16" height="22" rx="2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6"/><path d="M10 10h8M10 14h8M10 18h5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
    </span>
    <span class="path-num">01 · Before class</span>
    <h3>Lecture notes</h3>
    <p>Read the assigned textbook sections and, when assigned, run the Quarto notes. Those notes are in Quarto, so complete the setup instructions early. You need a working machine for the week to week flow of the course.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="path-card-proto accent-orange">
    <span class="path-icon" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" width="28" height="28" fill="none"><circle cx="11" cy="12" r="3.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6"/><circle cx="21" cy="12" r="3.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6"/><path d="M6 24c1.2-3.5 3.5-5 5-5s3.8 1.5 5 5M16 24c1.2-3.5 3.5-5 5-5s3.8 1.5 5 5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
    </span>
    <span class="path-num">02 · Monday</span>
    <h3>Concepts &amp; decisions</h3>
    <p> Mondays are for understanding the method, always starting from a business problem. You prepare a short introduction to that method and present it. I then take over and finish the lecture. The presentation schedule comes in week two, once enrollment is set.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="path-card-proto accent-green">
    <span class="path-icon" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" width="28" height="28" fill="none"><rect x="4" y="8" width="24" height="15" rx="2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6"/><path d="M10 26h12M12 14l2.5 2.5L19 12" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
    </span>
    <span class="path-num">03 · Wednesday</span>
    <h3>R lab</h3>
    <p>Wednesdays are labs, and we start from a problem, not from the code. The problem is posted before class. Come prepared. In class we work through guided notebooks: some of the code is already there, you complete the TODOs, we run it, and we interpret the output together. Then we argue the merits of the analysis and how to make it stronger.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="path-card-proto accent-cyan">
    <span class="path-icon" aria-hidden="true">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" width="28" height="28" fill="none"><path d="M8 22V10l8-4 8 4v12l-8 4-8-4z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M16 14v8M12 18h8" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>
    </span>
    <span class="path-num">04 · Outside class</span>
    <h3>Build and defend</h3>
    <p>For homework you get real data, a problem, and starter code. You turn in a notebook, at most six slides, and a video of at most five minutes — same story in all three. The project is individual and ends with an in-class presentation; details are in the syllabus.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```
